stemBlocks.value: Solve the simultaneous equations x + y = 6 and xy = 8.
Think first: Substitute from the linear equation into the product equation to get a quadratic in one variable.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p111-q06 from workbook page 111.

solutionSteps.instruction: Make y the subject of the linear equation.

contentBlocks.value: bring all terms to the right-hand side

strategyBlocks.value: Write y = 6 − x, substitute into xy = 8, rearrange to standard form, factorise and pair the roots.

whyThisWorks.value: Knowing a sum and a product of two numbers is exactly the information a quadratic encodes: the numbers are the roots of t² − (sum)t + (product) = 0, which is why x² − 6x + 8 = 0 appears here so directly. The two solutions are the same pair of numbers with the labels swapped, which is typical when the system is symmetric in x and y.

commonErrors.misconception: Assuming x = y because the equations look symmetric.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Assuming x = y because the equations look symmetric.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing x² + 6x + 8 = 0 through a sign slip when rearranging.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing x² + 6x + 8 = 0 through a sign slip when rearranging.

commonErrors.misconception: Reporting only one of the two ordered pairs.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reporting only one of the two ordered pairs.

examTip.value: If a system gives you a sum and a product, you can write the quadratic down immediately as t² − (sum)t + (product) = 0.
